title_prefix: RBF staging rebuilds every affected clus
mechanism: %RBF-STAGED-DIAGRAMS (src/mempool/txgraph.lisp:726-775) reconstructs rather than copies: for every affected cluster it re-adds each surviving transaction into a fresh TXGRAPH one at a time (txgraph-add-transaction), then replays %CLUSTER-REDUCED-EDGES one edge at a time through TXGRAPH-ADD-DEPENDENCY. Each cross-cluster TXGRAPH-ADD-DEPENDENCY pushes onto PENDING-DEPS and calls %RESOLVE-PENDING, which runs %MERGE-GROUP (rebuilding the merged cluster's depgraph from scratch and re-adding every reduced-parent edge) and then %CLUSTER-UPDATED, a full SFL relinearization -- so reconstructing one k-transaction cluster costs k merges and k relinearizations of a growing cluster instead of one copy. Core's staging is copy-on-write: PullIn makes the main cluster acceptable and then CopyToStaging assigns m_depgraph, m_mapping and m_linearization wholesale into a new cluster (refs/bitcoin/src/txgraph.cpp:1693-1706, 1221-1237), so the staged cluster is relinearized at most ONCE, under ACCEPTABLE_COST, and GetMainStagingDiagrams then only walks AppendChunkFeerates over the conflicting main clusters and the staging clusters (txgraph.cpp:2810-2834). rbf.cpp:64-68 states the intent explicitly: the 100-cluster rule-5 cap is what bounds 'how many mempool clusters might need to be re-sorted in order to process the replacement'. The exposure is real because of where the call sits: CHECK-RBF-RULES runs the diagram last among the RBF rules but BEFORE both script passes (src/validation/transaction.lisp:1216-1258, matching Core's order), and HANDLE-TX wraps the whole of tx handling in with-current-node-lock (src/networking/protocol.lisp:1836-1840).
consequence: One tx message can hold the node lock for ~0.4 s and never pay for it. Measured independently at exactly the rule-5 maximum shape -- 100 clusters (+max-rbf-replacement-candidates+ = 100, matching Core's MAX_REPLACEMENT_CANDIDATES) of 64 transactions (+max-cluster-count+ = 64, so 64 is the largest cluster that exists) with the replacement conflicting with each cluster's tail: 0.405 s and 0.403 s on two runs. 20 clusters of 64 cost 0.076 s, so it is linear in cluster count; 100 clusters of 8 cost 0.003 s, so it is superlinear (about k^2.4) in cluster size. Quantified against Core's per-cluster cost: our staging spends 3.6 ms per 64-transaction cluster while ONE linearize of the same 64-transaction chain depgraph costs 0.11 ms -- a ratio of 33x (22x at k=32, so the ratio grows with k) -- and one relinearization plus a memcpy is the whole of what Core pays after CopyToStaging. The attack is a ~200-byte tx message with a deliberately invalid signature: rules 3 and 4 gate only on the DECLARED fee, the diagram check runs before the script passes, and the transaction is then rejected, so it is never admitted, never relayed and never pays a fee -- repeatable at zero marginal cost, and defeating the rejects filter costs one nonce byte in an output. What holds it at S2 rather than S1 is the setup: about 6,400 planted mempool transactions in 100 chains of 64, plus a spendable UTXO large enough to declare a fee above the replaced set's total.
evidence: Probes under build/ga11v/p5-rbf-timing.lisp, run with scripts/dev.sh eval on the project container in worktree bl-ga11v-storage-s2, with bl.mp:*txgraph-shadow-checks* bound to NIL (the warm image loads the test system, which sets it to T, and the O(n) per-operation assert dominates otherwise). Sweep, one settled TXGRAPH-RBF-DIAGRAMS call before each timed one: (:CLUSTERS 100 :CLUSTER-SIZE 64 :TXS-IN-GRAPH 6400 :REMOVED 100 :STAGING-SECS 0.404999) and 0.402999 on the repeat; (:CLUSTERS 20 :CLUSTER-SIZE 64 :STAGING-SECS 0.076); (:CLUSTERS 100 :CLUSTER-SIZE 8 :STAGING-SECS 0.003); (:CLUSTERS 100 :CLUSTER-SIZE 1 :STAGING-SECS 0.0). Core-ratio probe timing 100 LINEARIZE calls on a 64-transaction chain depgraph against our own per-cluster staging cost at the same k: (:K 64 :ONE-LINEARIZE-SECS 1.1e-4 :OUR-PER-CLUSTER-STAGING-SECS 0.0036 :RATIO 32.7) and (:K 32 :ONE-LINEARIZE-SECS 3.0e-5 :OUR-PER-CLUSTER-STAGING-SECS 6.5e-4 :RATIO 21.7). Ours: src/mempool/txgraph.lisp:503,726-775,229,434,482; src/mempool/mempool.lisp:1188-1199,1229-1276; src/validation/transaction.lisp:1216-1258; src/networking/protocol.lisp:1836-1840. Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/txgraph.cpp:1221-1237,1693-1706,2810-2834; refs/bitcoin/src/policy/rbf.cpp:58-83; refs/bitcoin/src/policy/rbf.h:26.
fix_shape: Do not implement here. Port CopyToStaging rather than optimising the rebuild. %RBF-STAGED-DIAGRAMS should construct each scratch cluster by COPYING the live cluster's depgraph, mapping and linearization -- the three fields Core assigns in GenericClusterImpl::CopyToStaging -- into a new %CLUSTER installed directly in the scratch graph, then apply the removals to that copy (depgraph-remove-transactions plus the split the removal implies) and add only the candidate's dependencies, so each affected cluster is relinearized at most once and only when the removal or the candidate actually changed it. That needs a scratch-graph entry point that installs a prebuilt cluster without going through txgraph-add-transaction / txgraph-add-dependency and their %resolve-pending path, which is the whole source of the k merges. Two things the port must keep: our reduced-edge replay is what preserves the dependency closure today, so the copy has to bring the depgraph's ancestor/descendant closures across intact and be checked against the existing txgraph-vs-model equivalence tests; and Core caps a synchronous relinearization at ACCEPTABLE_COST (75,000) where LINEARIZE passes most-positive-fixnum, so the budget should come across with the copy or the per-cluster worst case stays unbounded. Pin the result with a timing assertion at the rule-5 maximum shape (100 x 64) that has a positive control -- a shape that is genuinely expensive for Core too -- so the ceiling cannot pass vacuously.
